task:
Build the final repository implementation for issue #540 so the self-hosted Octopus review service can be restored rapidly on `ed-finder-prod` before the legacy Hetzner host expires. Start from exact current origin/main `fd64ef8e14b5b026cec2d14949115ab681fb0b7d`. Read CLAUDE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, issue #540 and its comments, current old/new operator control-plane workflows/runbooks/tests, the complete prep branch `codex/run-33444386146-1` at `218f203ab48420919b929f9f0314700b27f15b9a`, and the completed investigation design from worker run `33445474584`. Use the prep branch as source material but reproduce the final coherent change on this isolated branch; do not modify the source branch. The wrapper will commit/push. Do not deploy, access either server, use real credentials, modify DNS/GitHub Apps, start/stop containers, connect to databases, or destroy legacy state in this worker. No ED-Finder/V3/Stage27/ratings/CRE/CPE/Journal product or data behavior changes.

Deadline/user decision superseding the prep branch: reuse the EXISTING Octopus external integration credentials and existing GitHub App for speed; do NOT require a new GitHub App. Fresh local-only secrets on the new host remain mandatory. The final implementation must fix two proven prep defects: `ENABLE_REVIEW_WORKERS` must default FALSE everywhere until explicit cutover, and the runbook must recommend reusing the existing App/credentials under this bounded deadline plan rather than creating a new App.

Keep and harden the good prep architecture: Octopus app exactly `ghcr.io/octopusreview/octopus-selfhost:1.0.122`, PostgreSQL 17 and Qdrant 1.17.0 dedicated volumes/networks, no public DB/Qdrant ports, web private at `127.0.0.1:43300`, bounded logging/resources/health checks, no coupling to any ED-Finder/V3 database/migration ledger. Fresh local secrets generated on target: `OCTOPUS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `OCTOPUS_DATA_KEY`, `OCTOPUS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; provider/GitHub integration credentials must never be generated or committed. Preserve prepare fail-closed behavior, atomic mode-0600 files, production hostname/root/confirmation gates, no start/migration during prepare.

Implement a secure OLD→NEW credential-transfer and cutover control plane. It must be auditable, allowlisted, fail closed and never move plaintext credentials through repository files, workflow inputs, command argv, GitHub logs, job outputs, or Actions artifacts. Prefer a three-phase encrypted handoff using pinned `age` with SHA-256 verification as identified by the investigation: (1) on `ed-new-operator`, generate a one-time X25519 identity and persist its private key only on the new host in a root-owned mode-0600 handoff directory; emit only the public recipient and a non-secret transfer id; ensure the prepared target env has fresh local-only secrets and `ENABLE_REVIEW_WORKERS=false`; (2) on legacy `hetzner-operator`, parse the old Octopus env with a strict non-executing dotenv parser, extract ONLY the approved external integration allowlist, copy/validate `ui.htpasswd` if present, encode canonical data, encrypt directly to the new public recipient, and upload/store only ciphertext with <=1-day retention; (3) on `ed-new-operator`, obtain ciphertext, decrypt only on the new host, strictly validate keys/types/sizes/PEM shape, atomically merge the allowlisted integrations into the new mode-0600 env, install htpasswd, verify required-key presence/shape without values, and destroy the one-time age identity/temporary plaintext. If Actions artifact transport is used, only ciphertext may be uploaded and best-effort deletion/short retention must be documented. If a direct SSH relay is safer within current control-plane constraints, implement that instead with equivalent no-plaintext-in-runner guarantees and explain why.

Approved external integration allowlist for reuse: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_APP_SLUG`, `GITHUB_STATE_SECRET`; optional provider keys may be copied only if the old deployment actually has them and the allowlist names them explicitly. Do NOT broadly copy Stripe/email/Slack/Jira/Linear/GitLab/Bitbucket/R2/Sentry/Microsoft secrets. Preserve multiline GitHub App PEM safely. Strict dotenv parser requirements: UTF-8; LF/CRLF; normal unquoted/single/double quoted values and multiline quoted PEM; limited deterministic escapes; reject NUL, malformed quoting, duplicate allowlisted keys, invalid names, unexpected continuation, multiple PEM blocks, oversized values; NEVER `source`, `eval`, shell-expand or echo values. If a required integration value is absent, fail with key NAME only.

CRITICAL SSH trust: new `ed-new-operator` already uses pinned `ED_NEW_OPERATOR_KNOWN_HOSTS`; preserve it. Secret-bearing legacy transfer must NOT use runtime `ssh-keyscan`. Require a new environment secret `HETZNER_OPERATOR_KNOWN_HOSTS` and verify the configured host:port with `ssh-keygen -F` exactly like the new lane. Do not fabricate/provision the value. Add a preflight operation that reports only `legacy_known_hosts_configured: true/false` and blocks transfer if missing. Existing non-secret old ops may remain unchanged only if required for compatibility, but all new secret-bearing paths must use pinned trust.

Implement bounded deployment operations on the NEW host, preferably through `.github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml` or a dedicated narrowly scoped workflow using `ed-new-operator`: `octopus-preflight`, `octopus-prepare`, `octopus-private-install`, `octopus-private-verify`, `octopus-enable-worker`, `octopus-cutover-verify` (names may differ but semantics must be clear). Trusted implementation must always be checked out from reviewed `main`, never a request branch. Operations must be idempotent/fail-closed and explicit.

Private install semantics: prepare `/opt/octopus`; pull pinned images; start only private Postgres/Qdrant first; apply the v1.0.122 Prisma migrations using the exact upstream tag/schema and a pinned toolchain without placing DB credentials in argv; then start web with review workers disabled; require local `/api/health` HTTP 200 and `/api/version` exactly `1.0.122`; require compose health green, persistence/restart proof, no listeners on 43332/43333/43334, and no mutation of existing V3/ED-Finder containers. If the migration tool requires a temporary repo checkout, verify tag commit `55583ac832472ad8b535f1f678f9c11837f7cfdb`, use pinned `oven/bun:1.3.4` plus the tag's lockfile/Prisma, and clean the checkout/temp env. Better if you can provide a deterministic migration helper script rather than error-prone runbook-only commands.

Reuse existing GitHub App: configure the transferred existing App vars on new host. `BETTER_AUTH_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` may remain private during private verification but must be changed to the final public `https://octopus.ed-finder.app` BEFORE enabling the GitHub webhook/review path if Octopus callback/signature generation depends on them. Fresh DB may need existing GitHub App installation/repository association to be re-linked through the private/public UI; document exact interactive step. Do not create or modify the GitHub App automatically. Existing webhook public URL can remain `https://octopus.ed-finder.app/api/github/webhook`; cutover moves the route underneath.

Single-worker cutover invariant: never allow both old and new review workers/webhooks to actively process PR events. Add explicit status/quiesce/enable operations or exact manual gates. Recommended sequence: fully private-verify new stack with workers false; freeze review triggers; quiesce old review worker while retaining old web/volumes for rollback; route `octopus.ed-finder.app` and webhook to new internal service using the NEW host's existing public edge, preferably without DNS change if hostname already points there; verify TLS/health/UI; re-link existing App installation in fresh DB; enable exactly one new worker; deliberately trigger one current-head test review; confirm bot identity, exact reviewed SHA, top-level/inline output as applicable, and no duplicate legacy delivery. Then re-trigger blocked #534/#536/#539 exact heads. Keep old host intact until proof; rollback disables new worker/route and re-enables old single worker.

Public edge: do not assume the old monolithic `config/nginx.conf` topology exists on ed-new. Inspect current repository V3 public-edge authority and design a minimal reversible route addition for `octopus.ed-finder.app` to the loopback/internal Octopus service. If repository authority is insufficient to safely automate edge routing, implement a read-only topology receipt plus a narrowly templated cutover script that fails closed unless expected new-host container/network/config fingerprints match. Do not change DNS in repository code. Record exact rollback.

Legacy retirement is NOT automatic. Implement only a status/quiesce helper plus documented later destruction procedure. Old DB/Qdrant are intentionally not migrated. After successful new exact-head review and bounded rollback interval, owner can stop/remove old compose/volumes/files before host expiry and revoke superseded local-only secrets. Existing external provider/App credentials remain valid by explicit user decision and may be rotated later.

Tests must be substantial and synthetic only: prep defaults workers false; compose isolation/no public DB ports/exact pins; secret generation/file modes/no logging; strict dotenv allowlist and multiline PEM; malformed/duplicate/oversize rejection with no values in errors; age public/private handoff contract and ciphertext-only artifact; pinned-old-known-hosts required; trusted-main implementation checkout; no request-branch execution; no secret in workflow outputs/argv/logging patterns; missing required external key fails by key name; private install order dependencies→migrate→web→health/version; migrations pinned to v1.0.122 tag commit/toolchain; no worker enable before private proof and old-quiesce receipt; exactly-one-worker cutover invariant; rollback path; public edge route only after proof; no ED-Finder/V3 DB/container mutation; no automated legacy destruction. Extend CI-stall/operator/repo-hygiene contracts as needed. Run focused pytest, Ruff/format, bash -n and shellcheck if available, parse all changed YAML with pinned PyYAML, `docker compose config` on synthetic env where available, static secret scan, `git diff --check`, and inspect final diff.

Also update issue/runbook truth: the actual historical Octopus 429 on PR #513 explicitly points to OpenAI platform billing; self-hosting removes Octopus hosted quota but not provider billing. Do not expose keys.

End with exact files, tests/results, operational phases now implemented, exact user input still required (expected only pinned old-host known_hosts if absent, provider billing/account action, and any interactive fresh-DB App/repo relink), and a rapid restoration checklist. No server write or cutover in this worker.
